v1.feedback: The yo-yo kinematics (drop, rubber-band stretch, squeeze, string particles, snap-back gold flash) are well-crafted and clearly idea-driven, but the piece is still the same LeePerrySmith head scan as its parent — the 'NEW BRANCH' mandate asks for more formal distance. The 9-unit drop likely sends the head below frame at rest camera z=14 with FOV 38; clamp the drop or auto-track camera Y so the full yo-yo arc stays composed. Consider a more radical swerve: e.g. fragment the head into tethered sub-masses that yo-yo independently (Zimoun-style mechanical repetition), or replace the literal head with an abstract form grown from the same point cloud — something that couldn't be mistaken for the parent with a uniform applied on top.

v2.feedback: The yo-yo concept genuinely drives the form — horizontal slicing with drop-and-snap mechanics and visible string lines is a clear conceptual swerve from a static head scan, not a rename. Two things to refine: the cascading slice drops risk fragmenting the head silhouette past quick readability, so consider reducing NUM_SLICES to 6-8 and keeping at least half the slices near-rest at any moment so the face remains legible as a face. The gold flash on snap-back is a nice touch but fires too diffusely across the whole slice; try concentrating it near the string attachment point (small radial falloff from slice center-x,z) so it reads as mechanical impact energy rather than uniform tint.
